notes.1: Most candidates answered this relatively straightforward question correctly, choosing C . This question relates to the function of book-keeping which is to record information.
notes.2: This question asked candidates to identify definitions of assets, liabilities, and capital. This question was fairly straightforward, being at the start of the question paper, and most candidates answered correctly. The correct answer is D . Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0452 Accounting June 2023
notes.7: This question tested candidates’ understanding of the effect of errors on the trial balance. Discount allowed of $900 was entered on the credit side of the trial balance instead of the debit side, and the bank overdraft of $750 was entered on the debit side instead of the credit side. The overall effect of this is that the total of the credit side is (900 × 2) – (750 × 2) = 300 more than the debit side. The correct answer is A .
notes.9: This question required candidates to identify whether each of the two stated errors needed a debit or a credit entry in the suspense account to correct them. They then had to use this information to calculate the original balance on the suspense account. The correct answer was B . Some candidates found this question challenging and selected an incorrect option.
notes.18: Candidates were required to select the correct double-entry for an amount received from a trade receivable after the debt had been written off. Most candidates correctly identified that the debit entry would be to the bank account, but some incorrectly thought that the credit entry would be to the account for irrecoverable receivables. The correct answer was A , i.e., the correct credit entry is to the debts recovered account.
notes.22: This question covered the topic of prepayments. Candidates were required to calculate the insurance charge for the year to 31 March 2023. The correct answer is B , i.e. (9/12 × 1680) + (3/12 × 1920) = 1740. While some candidates answered correctly, many selected an incorrect option.
notes.27: Candidates were required to select items which would be shown in the income and expenditure account for a sports club. The correct answer is C . Many candidates correctly identified that the depreciation and the subscriptions due would be shown in the income and expenditure account, but others selected an incorrect option. Notably, some candidates incorrectly thought that the purchase of new furniture would be shown in the income and expenditure account.
notes.28: This question covered the topics of clubs and societies. Candidates were asked to calculate the profit from a concert held by a music club. Most candidates found this question relatively straightforward and answered correctly. The correct answer is A .
notes.30: This question covered the topic of incomplete records. Candidates were asked to calculate the profit for the year using the available information. This figure is arrived at as follows: opening capital + profit – drawings = closing capital. The correct answer is B . It seems that some candidates found this question rather challenging, although a significant number of candidates did select the correct option.
notes.31: Candidates were required to calculate the figure for purchases. This may be calculated as follows: Closing trade payables + payments to credit suppliers + cash discount – opening trade payables. So, the correct answer is D . While some candidates selected the correct answer, others had not carried out this calculation correctly and selected an incorrect option. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0452 Accounting June 2023
notes.32: Question 32 asked candidates to calculate return on capital employed. This required them to know what is included in the figure for ‘return’ and for ‘capital employed’. The figure for return is profit before interest, and the figure for capital employed is the total of equity and debentures. The correct answer is B .
notes.33: Some candidates found Question 33 slightly challenging. It required candidates to identify a factor which would cause the liquid (acid test) ratio to decrease. The correct answer is D . While some candidates correctly identified this, others selected an incorrect option. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0452 Accounting June 2023
